From hair (work/prof/hair.json, the chair pilot). Why: tutoring is one-to-one sessions with a named tutor at a set time, at the business or at the student's home, with a card saved for a fee and charged at DONE. That is how hair runs. Yoga fits less: tutoring has no class seats or rosters, so its pack and weekly plan are added as branches here.
Usual side (flow A): sessions at Lee Learning Center, 220 College Ave. The old flowchart met in a library room the business uses, which reads closest to the business's own room. Flow B: Lee Home Tutoring at the student's home, 10 miles from 75 Grant St. Video is the third place in A4-01: it counts as at the center, same price, and the link goes to the parent's phone.
Names: Hannah and Marcus (center), Isaac and Nina (home). Alex M. books for his son Leo, 14 (A), and his daughter Ava, 16 (B). The master's second kind of work (electrical) is music lessons; the barbershop is the learning center; plumbing is home tutoring.
Prices, from the old flowchart's template and Sam's list: center math $35 (45 min), science $40, 15 more minutes $20, homework help for grades 1 to 5 $25, SAT math prep $55 and practice test $140 (both paid in full), a 4-session pack $130. Home: SAT or ACT prep $179 (2 h), math or science $85 (1 h), college essay help $150 (90 min, paid in full), practice test $199 (3 h); the $15 travel fee is inside every home price. A new student's first meeting is free: 20 minutes by video.
Money paths: A list|card|card (main: a card saved for the $20 fee, charged $35 at DONE on Saturday mornings, when Hannah opens alone), list|card|counter (paid at the front desk), list|full|none (SAT math prep paid in full). B list|card|card (main: card saved, $179 charged at DONE) and list|full|none (college essay help). Tutoring takes no hold and no deposit, and nothing is priced from photos or at the visit: those branches are off. The sign-up words (S1-13 to S1-16, S1-41 to S1-47) set the services this way.
The free first meeting is a first step (A4-43, B4-38), not a money path: Leo and Ava have theirs on file. A pack session (A5-03, A5-22), a weekly plan (A4-30, B4-44) and a test-prep series (A4-31, B4-45) are branches; each session is paid like a single one.
The old flowchart sold single sessions only (Jay's old answer J20). Jay has since said no rule from before binds, and tutors really sell prepaid packs and weekly sessions, so the 4-session pack ($130, paid in full) and the weekly plan stay. A pack's prepay limit, written agreement and right to cancel come from the state form (pf.rules). The gap 'Offered only off Rosie' came only from J20, so it was dropped (review Oct 23).
Child safety: a parent books for a student under 18. Age, grade, school and learning needs are typed only on the secure page (B4-32 shows the screen), never through the AI or a text. Texts, codes, video links and progress notes go to the parent. At home an adult stays the whole session (B4-26), and the tutor waits outside if only the student answers (B8-09). At the center a student 12 or older may be dropped off and goes home only with an approved adult (A8-67, A8-42).
